summary: Today’s PaymentsDive recap: 8 new stories, with focus on regulation, product + fintech innovation.

articles.title: Visa, Mastercard urge court to approve fee settlement
articles.description: The card networks contend Walmart and trade groups want to scuttle a legal pact over card swipe fees using recycled arguments the court has rejected.

articles.title: Congress should examine EWA bill
articles.description: “Combining employer-integrated solutions and direct-to-consumer products under a single, relaxed standard weakens consumer safety,” writes an industry executive.

articles.title: Credit card debt ticks up
articles.description: Consumers have been grappling with rising credit card interest rates and ballooning balances in the past few years, a recent Fed survey found.

articles.title: Stripe agentic commerce revs up
articles.description: The digital payment juggernaut’s agentic commerce activity went “vertical” last month, President John Collison said this week.

articles.title: Fiserv ‘reset’ bolsters case, litigants say
articles.description: The processing giant has no basis for a shareholder lawsuit to be dismissed, given its own comments, investors suing the company told a judge this week.

articles.title: Businesses view stablecoins warily
articles.description: Despite the hype surrounding the digital assets, businesses remain cool to using the cryptocurrency, according to the results of a Cleveland Federal Reserve survey.

articles.title: JPMorgan rounds up partners
articles.description: The biggest U.S. bank has been collecting payments partners to better integrate software and keep up with industry trends, among other purposes.

articles.title: Upgrade applies for ILC charter
articles.description: The decade-old credit-card startup named a SoFi alum and longtime regulator as CEO of its proposed bank.
